$snippet: knowledge/snippets/Slider.reference.html — the second div.field[data-type=double]: div.rail > div.track + input#r2-lo + input#r2-hi (#313 lane B123)

props_add.name: valueLow
props_add.$note: The low handle's current value. Clamped so it can never exceed valueHigh (authored JS, see behaviour).

props_add.name: valueHigh
props_add.$note: The high handle's current value. Clamped so it can never fall below valueLow.

props_add.name: unit
props_add.$note: Prefix/suffix for the displayed value pair, e.g. '£'. Specimen shows GBP; not itself a currency-formatting component.

props_add.name: disabled
props_add.$note: NOT DRAWN as a specimen this pass — the gated Slider has no disabled specimen either; carried as a declared gap, not invented here to avoid drifting ahead of its own precedent.

props_note: valueLow/valueHigh apply when type = double; the single type keeps `value`.
variants_double_use: Two handles on one track, a min/max range: two native range inputs on one rail, clamped so they never cross, the last-touched on top, each named by aria-valuetext ('£200, minimum'), the pair shown as text.

anatomy_add.$note: under the double field: the rail (div.rail) holds a DRAWN track (div.track, an element here, not the browser's) and two inputs, each with its own thumb — consistent with L4's track and thumb parts (the double type has two thumbs on one track).
parts: track (div.track, aria-hidden, the two-stop fill band --lo..--hi)

accessibility_add.role: Two real <input type="range"> elements, each with its own aria-labelledby (sharing the field's one visible label) and a live aria-valuetext ('£200, minimum' / '£800, maximum') so AT never has to infer which handle is which from position alone.
accessibility_add.keyboard: Native — Arrow keys/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown operate whichever handle has focus, exactly as the gated Slider's single handle does. No custom keydown handler was authored; the browser's own range-input keyboard model is reused twice.
accessibility_add.valueText: aria-valuetext is recomputed on every input event for BOTH handles (the low handle's text also changes near the clamp boundary), and the visible value pair mirrors it as plain text — never colour or handle position alone (1.4.1), the same answer the gated Slider gives.
accessibility_add.clamp: The low handle cannot be dragged/keyed past the high handle and vice versa (authored JS). The clamp is silent (no error message) — DECIDED here as a UX default, not settled: should crossing produce a message, or is silent clamping sufficient? See $decisionsForDave.

antiPatterns_add: Letting the low handle's DOM z-index get permanently trapped under the high handle at a shared value — the is-top class swap on pointerdown exists specifically to prevent this

Synthesising a single custom control with two drawn thumbs instead of two real range inputs — the two-native-inputs technique is what earns the keyboard model honestly, at the cost of the clamp needing to be authored
decisionsForDave_carried: Should crossing the clamp boundary produce a message (e.g. a brief inline note) or stay a silent clamp, as built?
Slider's own meta records a DEPRECATED tick-marker token finding — should Range slider inherit tick markers at all, or stay bare (as built)?
Is £/GBP the right specimen currency, or should the canonical specimen be currency-neutral (a plain numeric range) with money shown only in a usage example?
when_note: Under s272-D36 (filters and settings, where the change takes effect at once; a committed value is paired with a number field) and s272-D40 (under about five steps, selection controls instead) — the same rules as the single type.
